newsitem.title: UK: Gift for new Oxford business school in jeopardy.
newsitem.headline: Gift for new Oxford business school in jeopardy.

text.p: A Middle Eastern businessman was reconsidering a 20 million pound ($33 million) gift to Oxford University for a business school on Wednesday after professors voted against building it on a sports ground.

The Times newspaper said Wafic Said, a Syrian-born financier who made his fortune in the construction boom in Saudi Arabia in the 1970s and 1980s, would consult the university and his trustees before making a final decision.
A congregation of Oxford dons voted 259 to 214 against backing the project. Some of them expressed reservations about Said's motives, the newspaper said.
"The vote calls into question the congregation's commitment to developing a world-class business school. In light of this I shall obviously need to consider my benefaction," Said told The Times.

He announced the donation, the biggest single gift to the to Oxford University in 50 years, in July. The university, one of the world's most presitigious centres of learning, said then it hoped the new school would be open in two years.
